previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a male with a history of alcoholic cirrhosis, hepatitis C, and esophageal varices, was admitted after presenting with hematemesis and bloody stools. He was found to have a low hemoglobin and was transfused one unit of packed red blood cells. An endoscopy revealed a bleeding arteriovenous malformation in the antrum, which was successfully treated with argon plasma coagulation. His abdominal pain improved with tramadol, and his blood pressure was controlled by restarting lisinopril and continuing nadolol. He was monitored for alcohol withdrawal using the CIWA scale, which resolved without medication. The patient left the hospital against medical advice before a follow-up CBC was reviewed but was discharged on oral PPI, antihypertensives, and supportive medications with instructions to avoid alcohol and follow up with his primary and liver specialists.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old man with HCV/EtOH cirrhosis with non-bleeding 
esophageal varices (EGD ___, colonic AVM ___ ___ with 
recurrent admissions for GI bleed, presenting with report of 
increased black stools with bloody streaks and coffee ground 
emesis, Hgb drop from 9.2 to 7.9 since ___. 

ACUTE ISSUES
# GIB: Report of melanotic stool with streaks of blood, as well 
as coffee ground emesis. Brown stool noted on rectal exam, and 
no melanotic stools or hematemesis observed this admission. 
Likely slow bleed, though had Hgb drop since last testing 
earlier this month. Has known gastric and colonic AVMs, internal 
hemorrhoids, as well as grade I-II varices, that could be 
sources for blood loss. Maintained on octreotide gtt, PO PPI and 
IV CTX. Underwent EGD which showed no evidence of active 
bleeding, only small erosions. Nadolol held initially in setting 
of acute bleed, but restarted at discharge. Patient remained 
hemodynamically stable throughout the admission and did not 
require trasnfusions. Hgb at discharge 8.2.

# Abdominal pain: Distractable exam, LFTs at baseline. No hx of 
SBP and no ascites on exam. Improved prior to discharge. 

# ETOH/HCV cirrhosis: Child A, MELD 12. Decompensated by 
non-bleeding Grade I-II varices (___). No ascites, no history 
of encephalopathy. Not on transplant list given active EtOH use. 
Held nadalol given concern for bleed on admission, but resumed 
at discharge.    
 
# HTN: Held BP meds (lisinopril, nadolol) in the setting of 
presumed GIB on admission, but resumed at discharge.  

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES
- Medications changed: decreased dose of both nadolol and 
lisinopril. Please consider stopping lisinopril and swithcing to 
other anti-hypertensive, as ACEi should be avoided in patient 
with cirrhosis. 
- Consider outpatient colonoscopy, as patient has known AVMs and 
no source of bleeding was identified on EGD.
